claims.text: A hybrid high-throughput DSC and CALPHAD method can accurately determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, melting-volume change, and selected liquid thermodynamic properties across the HEA family.
The hybrid method can determine these properties efficiently.
The intended materials are as-cast, near-equiatomic HEAs with complex multielement compositions.
CALPHAD models calibrated against binary and ternary subsystems can predict complete fusion thermodynamics and liquid-phase behavior in HEAs.
Configurational entropy in HEAs mediates the relationship between atomic-scale mixing and macroscopic phase-transition behavior.
The configurational-entropy-mediated behavior is captured by both DSC measurements and CALPHAD predictions.
DSC directly and reliably measures heat flow associated with solidus and melting events.
HEAs exhibit a rapid increase in heat capacity at the solidus.
CALPHAD uses existing thermodynamic data to estimate property trends over a wide composition space.
Using DSC data to validate and recalibrate CALPHAD predictions reduces the uncertainties of both methods.
The hybrid approach will estimate melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting-volume change to within approximately ±10–15% of exhaustive conventional measurements.
The method will reliably predict melting-temperature depression caused by configurational entropy across HEA composition space.
Standalone DSC measurements of multicomponent HEAs have considerable uncertainty because of complex phase behavior.
CALPHAD predictions for HEAs can be unreliable when databases lack sufficiently assessed constituent subsystems.
The hybrid approach reduces the limitations of standalone DSC and standalone CALPHAD.
The approach is primarily applicable when relevant binary and ternary thermodynamic assessments are available.
Performance may be limited by poorly characterized interactions, incomplete multicomponent databases, or inadequate DSC resolution and calibration.
Thermal expansion, dilatometry, or density measurements can provide the melting-volume change needed for validation.
Discrepancies exceeding ±15% for a majority of tested alloys, or failure to reproduce the expected composition trends, would falsify the method.

contradictions.description: The proposed method is defined as DSC plus CALPHAD and is claimed to determine melting-volume change, but the validation design requires an additional dilatometry or density method to obtain that quantity. Thus the stated two-component method does not itself cover every claimed output.

The accuracy claim is relative to exhaustive conventional experiments, whereas the falsification rule tests disagreement between DSC measurements and CALPHAD predictions. Disagreement between the two hybrid components is not equivalent to demonstrating that the final calibrated hybrid estimate exceeds the claimed error against an independent reference.
